probe.text_sample: Working with the light a room already has | Maren Vik Skip to content Bergen --:--:-- Maren Vik, home Work Services About Journal Contact Overview Menu Work Services About Journal Contact Overview Available from November Journal Working with the light a room already has Why I stopped bringing strobes to most shoots, and what a window can do that a softbox can't. 12 May 2026 , 1 min read, light , process For years I arrived on set with two cases of lights. Now I arrive with a reflector, a roll of black fabric and a lot of patience. Read the room first Before I unpack anything I spend twenty minutes watching where the light falls and how fast it moves. Most rooms have one good wall and one good hour. The job is to find both. Shape, don’t add A white card to lift a shadow, a black flag to deepen one. That’s usually all it takes. The light stays soft and the pictures look like the place they were made in. When I still use flash Late winter afternoons in Bergen, and product shots where colour has to be exact.
